youtube_title: Drumright, Oklahoma: the outlaw federal agents freed, 1924 (Drumright request)
youtube:
You asked for Drumright! In the 1920s, federal agents investigating the Osage murders, a time that came to be called the Reign of Terror, let a bank robber named Blackie Thompson out to work as their informant. He went back to robbing banks. On July 2, 1924, a bank in nearby Avery was robbed; four officers went after the robbers in one car, and near Drumright the robbers opened fire. Police Chief Jack Ary was wounded and Officer Ulysses Sterling Lenox, 38, was killed. Thompson kept robbing banks; in July 1934 he broke out of death row in Texas, and that December he was shot dead in a gunfight with officers near Amarillo. Thompson appears in David Grann's Killers of the Flower Moon and in the 2023 film. Comment your town, and it could be next! #Drumright #CreekCounty #Oklahoma #History #LaPorteAfterDark #Shorts

All pictures are drawn; the bank, the cars, the jail and the prison wall are drawn generic, since no pictures of them are known. Narration is a computer voice. Sources: Oklahoma Law Enforcement Memorial (oklemem.com); Officer Down Memorial Page; Wikipedia, "Blackie Thompson"; History.com and PBS NewsHour on David Grann's reporting; Encyclopaedia Britannica and FBI.gov on the Osage murders; Tony Perrin, RevolverGuy (2023); Texas Prison Board minutes, July 24, 1934 (Texas State Library); The Memphis (Tex.) Democrat, Dec. 7, 1934. The sources disagree on whether anyone was ever convicted of Officer Lenox's murder, so this doesn't say. More LaPorte County history: https://laporteweathernow.com/history

You asked for Drumright!
Federal agents freed an outlaw to help them catch killers. Instead, he became one.
In the 1920s, Osage people in Oklahoma were being murdered for their oil wealth, a time that came to be called the Reign of Terror. The Bureau of Investigation, the agency that became the FBI, let a bank robber named Blackie Thompson out to work as its informant. He went back to robbing banks.
On July 2, 1924, a bank in nearby Avery was robbed, and word came the robbers were headed toward Drumright. Four officers went after them, all in one car. Near Drumright, the robbers opened fire. Police Chief Jack Ary was wounded. Officer Ulysses Sterling Lenox, 38, was killed.
Thompson kept robbing banks. In July 1934 he broke out of death row in Texas, and that December he was shot dead in a gunfight with officers near Amarillo. He appears in David Grann's Killers of the Flower Moon and in the 2023 film.
LaPorte After Dark. More LaPorte County history: laporteweathernow.com/history
